exercises.q: Don't worry, I ___ (will help/am helping) you with the boxes.
Look at those dark clouds. It ___ (is going to/will) rain.
We ___ (are meeting/will meet) Jana at 7 tonight – it's all arranged.
The train ___ (leaves/is leaving) at 6.45 tomorrow morning, according to the timetable.
I'm not sure, but I ___ (might/must) go to the gym later.
You ___ (mustn't/don't have to) smoke in the hospital. It's forbidden.
It's Saturday, so you ___ (don't have to/mustn't) get up early.
You look tired. You ___ (should/must to) go to bed earlier.
When I was five, I ___ (could/can) already read.
She ___ (has to/have to) wear a uniform at work.
___ (Could/Must) you open the window, please?
I think robots ___ (will do/are doing) most of the housework in the future.
I've decided: I _____ (learn) to drive next year.
exercises.a: am going to learn | 'm going to learn

exercises.q: _____ you _____ (do) anything this weekend? – Yes, I'm visiting my parents.
Last week I _____ (have to) work late every day.
You _____ (not need) to bring anything – we've got plenty of food.
exercises.a: don't need | do not need | needn't | need not

exercises.q: I'm hungry. – OK, I _____ (make) you a sandwich.
I will to call you tomorrow.
You must to wear a helmet.
He can swims very well.
Maybe I go to the cinema tonight.
exercises.a: Maybe I will go to the cinema tonight. | I might go to the cinema tonight. | Maybe I'll go to the cinema tonight.

exercises.a: You should sleep more. | You should get more sleep. | You ought to sleep more.

exercises.a: You mustn't park here. | You must not park here. | You can't park here. | You cannot park here.

exercises.q: Who will pack the computers?
exercises.text: Next month our company is moving to a new office on the other side of the city. The move is going to happen over one weekend, so nobody will have to work in a half-empty building. Staff don't have to pack their own computers – a professional company will do that – but everyone must clear their desks by Friday afternoon. The new office has a canteen and a gym, so many of us might start exercising at lunchtime. The only problem is parking: there are only forty spaces, so most people will have to come by public transport.

exercises.q: When will Eva arrive at the party?
exercises.text: Dear Jana, thanks for your message. Yes, I'd love to come to your birthday party on Saturday! I'm working until three, but I can be at your place by five. Should I bring anything? I could make my famous chocolate cake, or I might just bring a bottle of wine – let me know what you prefer. By the way, I'm going to take the train, so I won't have to worry about driving home. See you soon! Eva
